learnItems.title: Anger
learnItems.summary: Gurbani does not treat anger as honest fire. It shows the deeper illness of ego, then points the hot mind toward Hukam, the Guru's Shabad, humble company, and speech held inside Truth.

learnItems.title: Anxiety
learnItems.summary: Gurbani answers that trembling by naming the One who creates, nourishes, protects, and receives the restless question before it multiplies.

learnItems.title: Attachment
learnItems.summary: Gurbani loosens attachment by putting every gift back inside Hukam. In the Lord's sanctuary, praise and blame, gain and loss, nearness and separation stop being masters of the soul.

learnItems.title: Comparison
learnItems.summary: Gurbani loosens comparison by moving the eye from possession to Hukam: contentment becomes the earring, praise becomes the mind’s labor, and every breath returns to the One who gives without shortage.

learnItems.title: Conduct
learnItems.summary: Gurbani makes conduct concrete: Naam joined to pure action, holy company washing the dirty mind, honest labor with open hands, and seva done without reward.

learnItems.title: Control
learnItems.summary: Gurbani does not shame faithful effort; it returns effort to its rightful size. Power, gifts, liberation, and the outcome of every breath remain held in Hukam, not in the anxious grip.

learnItems.title: Discipline
learnItems.summary: Gurbani makes discipline concrete: contentment worn inwardly, Naam repeated in the heart, honest work, and truth carried like wealth that will go with the soul.

learnItems.title: Doubt
learnItems.summary: Gurbani does not treat doubt as proof of depth. It names the fire directly: roaming does not quench it, inner filth does not clear by changing scenery, and wavering loses authority when the Guru’s word is allowed to abide within.

learnItems.title: Ego
learnItems.summary: Gurbani names haumai as chronic illness, not strength. Its cure is not self-hatred but grace that brings the Guru’s Shabad into practice until conduct, speech, service, and humility no longer orbit the self.

learnItems.title: Exhaustion
learnItems.summary: Gurbani answers the worn-out heart by moving it from frantic motion into received care: holy company cools the body and mind, the Guru becomes mother and father, and the Creator who made the life is trusted to sustain it.

learnItems.title: Fear
learnItems.summary: Gurbani does not ask the frightened heart to act brave on its own. It brings fear under merciful keeping: the Creator protects, Naam cools the mind, holy company roots out the assault, and the Guru’s Shabad teaches fear to lose its throne.

learnItems.title: Forgiveness
learnItems.summary: Gurbani names forgiveness beside conduct and contentment, then shows the fearful heart becoming free through the Fearless One. Forgiveness is not denial; it is the discipline that stops bitterness from becoming the shape of the soul.

learnItems.title: Gratitude
learnItems.summary: Gurbani restores gratitude by telling the truth about dependence: pain can become medicine, comfort can dull longing, and unrecognized mercy can become living Naam when the Guru opens the heart.

learnItems.title: Greed
learnItems.summary: The Guru changes the question from what can be gained to what can be carried. False trade makes the mind and body false; praise, truthful labor, sharing, and Naam become the wealth that leaves the soul lighter rather than trapped.

learnItems.title: Honesty
learnItems.summary: Gurbani makes honesty larger than blunt accuracy. Truth becomes livable when Naam cleans conduct, Sangat washes the dirty mind, the hand works and gives, and remembrance reaches the mouth and the walk.

learnItems.title: Hukam
learnItems.summary: Gurbani does not ask for passive resignation. It places body, soul, honor, mercy, and the next step inside Hukam so the ego can stop acting like the author of reality.

learnItems.title: Loneliness
learnItems.summary: Gurbani meets loneliness with a path, not a platitude. The soul searches mind and body, asks for a saintly friend to show the Beloved, enters Sat Sangat where the Lord abides, and learns that the humble are kept close to the One who cherishes them as children.

learnItems.title: Mercy
learnItems.summary: Gurbani shows mercy as the Lord’s gift, the way longing is led into Sangat, and the nearness by which the humble are cherished. Mercy is not softness without truth; it is the sustaining reality that lets return happen at all.

learnItems.title: Patience
learnItems.summary: Gurbani makes patience active and wealthy. The mind's wandering ceases in the Society of the Saints, mercy lights the mind, true bankers trade in Naam, and patience, honor, and glory ripen in those who listen to the Name.

learnItems.title: Purpose
learnItems.summary: The cited shabads make purpose concrete. Human birth is given as a chance to meet the Lord; the path is recognized in honest labor and sharing; lasting profit is what can accompany the soul beyond the day.

learnItems.title: Restlessness
learnItems.summary: Gurbani does not shame the search; it asks where the search finally bows. Roaming cools when the Shabad gathers the double mind, saintly company gives the heart a place to stay, and service turns seeking into remembered love.

learnItems.title: Sangat
learnItems.summary: Gurbani makes sangat a place of divine nearness. In Sat Sangat the path is asked honestly, the Lord is found, ego loosens, and the mind and body cool from restless searching into remembrance.

learnItems.title: Seeking
learnItems.summary: Gurbani dignifies longing and then gives it a home: Sat Sangat where the Lord abides, the Guru's word that extinguishes doubt, and remembrance that stops postponing devotion.

learnItems.title: Self-Worth
learnItems.summary: Gurbani steadies worth by rooting it in Hukam, Guru-given Naam, Truth, and the Lord who keeps the humble close. Dignity is not performed into existence; it is received and then lived truthfully.

learnItems.title: Seva
learnItems.summary: Gurbani places seva under the Guru: the servant does not advertise the self, keeps Naam in the heart, sells the mind to the True Guru, and serves without reward until the Lord—not recognition—becomes the aim.

learnItems.title: Shame
learnItems.summary: Gurbani answers shame with mercy, service, and the Lord’s shelter. The child can tell the truth about mistakes because the Forgiving One is still Father, Mother, Patron, and refuge.

learnItems.title: Softness
learnItems.summary: Gurbani forms softness through Naam, sweet speech, humble walking, Hukam, and conquest of the mind. Gentleness is not weakness; it is truth delivered after ego has been lowered.

learnItems.title: Speech
learnItems.summary: The cited shabads do more than recommend politeness. They make speech a spiritual test: harshness brings grief, slander dirties the mouth, and remembrance becomes real when it sweetens the tongue and humbles the walk.

learnItems.title: Reverence begins where measurement fails
learnItems.summary: This shabad dismantles the habit of auditing holiness from the outside. The Brahm Giani cannot be priced, fully described, or reduced to a public rank, because a life saturated with God carries a depth only God-consciousness can truly know.

learnItems.title: Do not spend a passing life on a dirty tongue
learnItems.summary: This shabad speaks to the body as if waking it from a dangerous dream. Comfort, gossip, lust, hoarding, theft, and display all look powerful for a moment, but only truthful deeds and the sweetness of Naam remain when the soul has to leave.

learnItems.title: Do not murder the soul by wasting a rare life
learnItems.summary: This shabad treats human birth as a rare trust, not a casual backdrop for entertainment. Without Naam, eating, laughing, showing off, and even staying alive become hollow; with the GurMantra planted inside, the heart finally holds what the life was given for.

learnItems.title: Belonging is not private property
learnItems.summary: This pauree breaks open the possessive mind. All are Yours, You belong to all, and everyone begs from the same inexhaustible Source. The ego has no independent ground to stand on; even the place from which it asks is given by the One it depends on.

learnItems.title: The highest religion becomes visible in conduct
learnItems.summary: This shabad refuses to let religion remain an identity, performance, or ritual résumé. The highest path is Naam joined to clean conduct, the finest ritual is the dirty mind washed in holy company, and the sweetest speech is praise that actually lives on the tongue.

learnItems.title: Worldly greatness carries anxiety inside it
learnItems.summary: This shabad punctures the impressive surface of worldly power. The people who look great are still afflicted by anxiety, the landlord still fights over land he must leave, and only loving attachment to the Lord gives greatness that is not already sick with loss.

learnItems.title: Appetite grows into a life unless the Guru interrupts it
learnItems.summary: This shabad traces craving from infancy to death with unsentimental precision — milk, family, play, food, sexual desire, wealth, anger, decline, cremation. The pattern is not harmless just because it is familiar; without the Guru, the soul is left asking where to go as the world drowns.

learnItems.title: Take the scattered question to the Guru
learnItems.summary: This shabad begins with honest confusion — whom shall I serve, what shall I chant? The answer is not more spiritual shopping, but accepting the True Guru’s will, uprooting selfishness, guarding the field of the mind, and letting Naam and Shabad make peace real.

learnItems.title: Bow until wandering stops asking for the lead
learnItems.summary: This brief shabad begins in full prostration before the All-powerful Lord. It does not stay ceremonial: the bow becomes a direct cry for protection from wandering and for the Lord's own hand.

learnItems.title: Choose the wealth that endures
learnItems.summary: Guru Nanak turns the language of trade toward the soul: not every profit is worth carrying. Praise, truth, and Naam are the wealth that remains when false dealing falls away.

learnItems.title: Center hope where the wandering mind cannot rule
learnItems.summary: This shabad opens by showing the God-conscious being resting hope in the One alone. It turns the heart toward gathered hope, disciplined mind, and shared remembrance.

learnItems.title: Longing is led home in saintly company
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens in aching longing for the Beloved and admits it cannot find the way alone. It searches mind and body, turns toward saintly company, and keeps asking to be brought near.

learnItems.title: Cling to the One until the mind cools
learnItems.summary: The pauree begins by praising those who release every other hold and cling to the One alone. It sets side by side Maya-drunk unrest with the peace and sweetness that arise in saintly company and Naam.

learnItems.title: Wear contentment before you speak of conquest
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by taking visible yogic marks and turning them inward — contentment, humility, meditation, remembrance. It opens into brotherhood and comes to rest where true conquest happens, in the mind rather than the room.

learnItems.title: Conquer the self before you fight the world
learnItems.summary: This shabad opens by naming the true battlefield as the soul itself. It directs the heart toward Hukam, inner victory, and the peace that follows self-conquest.

learnItems.title: Deeper fearlessness comes by tasting Naam
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with the strange claim that speaking the Unspoken becomes nectar. It carries the listener through lesser fears falling away, recognition through the Guru's Shabad, and hearts filled with the Lord's essence.

learnItems.title: Rest where praise and possession lose their force
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by locating rest in the Lord's sanctuary. It then equalizes pleasure and pain, gold and copper, praise and slander, until attachment loses the right to name reality.

learnItems.title: Do not forget the One who never forgets you
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with a repeated question — why forget the One who sees, gives, sustains, and rescues? It moves from gratitude into recognition, and ends with the humble servant holding remembrance instead of transactional effort.

learnItems.title: Do not postpone remembrance
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by exposing the delaying mind that keeps waiting for the right time to remember the Lord. It responds with day-and-night attunement and devotion that does not forget the Beloved even briefly.

learnItems.title: Duality makes decoration hollow
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by calling the life deceived by duality cursed and unstable like a wall of sand. It travels through the uselessness of decoration without the Beloved and ends where beauty becomes real only by being pierced with the Shabad.

learnItems.title: Ego is a chronic illness with a cure inside it
learnItems.summary: Guru Angad does not flatter ego or mystify it. He names it as the pattern behind action and bondage, then says the cure appears through grace and the Guru's Shabad.

learnItems.title: Everything becomes whole when Naam lives inside
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by calling the path and cleansing bath perfect when the Name is in the heart. It keeps extending that wholeness through peace, contentment, yoga, glory, and the Creator's presence.

learnItems.title: Doubt does not die by wandering
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by saying the fire of doubt is not quenched by roaming. It turns the mind toward the Guru's word, saintly company, and the surrender of selfishness until peace merges like water in water.

learnItems.title: Fear leaves when schemes do
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens with rescue arriving alongside subdued ego. It travels through useless plans being abandoned, fear leaving by meeting the True One, and ends in the genuine merchandise recognized through the Guru.

learnItems.title: Forgiveness is the fast that makes one fearless
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by naming forgiveness, good conduct, and contentment as the real fast. It travels through release from disease and death-fear and comes to rest in the Lord already present within and without.

learnItems.title: Forgiveness settles into lasting peace
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with the Perfect Guru's completed work — forgiveness given, peace found. It opens wider into peace spreading everywhere and comes to rest in singing the Guru's Bani and meditating on Naam.

learnItems.title: Fresh Naam enters the mind
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens by promising freedom from the old cycle through meeting the True Guru. It moves through understanding given by the Shabad and rests in the ever-fresh Naam abiding within the mind.

learnItems.title: Fruitful service gives the life a path
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens by calling service to the Lord fruitful and honorable. It travels through meeting the Guru, finding the Lord through the Shabad, and rejecting stubbornness as a path to discovery.

learnItems.title: God-consciousness is received, not staged
learnItems.summary: This section opens by saying the God-conscious being knows God and loves the One alone. It keeps insisting that such stature is given by God Himself, which means greatness, purity, and fearlessness cannot be self-manufactured.

learnItems.title: Mercy remembered becomes living Naam
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens in confession — I did not recognize what You did for me. It moves through unworthiness and pity received, then blooms when the True Guru is met and Naam makes body and mind green again.

learnItems.title: Holy company breaks the crowded heat inside
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with the body crowded by desire and anger, then shows what changes when the Holy Saint is actually met. It turns from the thorn of ego and wandering pain toward humility, sanctuary, and peace supported by Naam.

learnItems.title: Holy company washes deeper than self-scrubbing
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens by calling the sight of the saints a perfect cleansing bath. It travels through ego falling away, the One becoming visible everywhere, and the heart being irrigated with Naam.

learnItems.title: Honor the one through whom life arrives
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by tracing birth, friendship, marriage, and lineage through woman. It then asks how she can be called bad when kings themselves are born from her, and ends in radiant mouths that praise the Lord.

learnItems.title: Hope in the Lord outlives the world's reach
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by describing the one held so closely by the Lord that stain and worldly pressure cannot settle. It moves through freedom from anxiety and pain, then ends in the Guru who shows the Perfect Lord.

learnItems.title: Hukam is the atmosphere of everything
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by placing form, life, greatness, pain, blessing, and wandering inside Hukam. It keeps widening that field until nothing stands outside the Command and ego has nowhere left to boast.

learnItems.title: Human birth is a chance, not an ornament
learnItems.summary: The shabad refuses to flatter human life; it names it as a rare opening to meet the Lord while breath is still here. It moves from opportunity to urgency, pressing the hearer toward Naam, sangat, and a life that answers the chance it was given.

learnItems.title: Humble company ends the fight underneath the fight
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by saying that meeting the humble defeats the messenger of death. It pushes deeper through the Lord dwelling in the mind, worldly entanglements ending, and the Guru's grace becoming ambrosial Naam.

learnItems.title: Learning without inward turning stays trapped in Maya
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by criticizing scholars who read and shout while remaining attached to Maya. It pushes further by exposing teaching without contemplation and ends in the waste of a life spent repeating what was never inwardly recognized.

learnItems.title: Let humility become the strength that does no harm
learnItems.summary: This section keeps describing the God-conscious being as dust of all, kind to all, harmful to none, impartial, and nectar-bearing. It turns humility into a presence from which no injury comes.

learnItems.title: Let the Name become your family
learnItems.summary: This section opens by describing the God-conscious being as one who loves the One alone and lives in that nearness. It keeps narrowing support down to Naam, until even family, wakefulness, and permanence are redefined by it.

learnItems.title: The humble are kept close
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens with the Guru as great giver, planting the Lord within the heart. It carries the listener through hearing the Guru's teaching, exposing lesser cravings, and ends with the Lord holding His humble servant close like a cherished child.

learnItems.title: Love fills the minds and bodies of the devoted
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with love rising inside the mind and body as a real hunger for darshan and holy company. It asks for one mercy only, the grace to chant Naam, and ends by widening the heart into the Lord's presence everywhere.

learnItems.title: Love the Guru with mind and body
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by fastening mind and body to the Guru in love. It broadens through obedience, Sangat, and the dust-like poverty of Maya-attachment, then ends in total remembrance: this life, body, and breath are Yours.

learnItems.title: Love the true treasure before desire names your wealth
learnItems.summary: The pauree opens by commanding love for the Lord as the true treasure. It answers desire, fear, and the fantasy of lasting wealth by saying the Name alone accompanies and enlightens.

learnItems.title: Make Naam the work of your life
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by giving the saints a clear assignment — let Naam be the real work. It presses past distraction, calling for remembrance, shared encouragement, and the peace that even the drowning can find in the treasure of the Name.

learnItems.title: Make the body honorable by what it serves
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by blessing words that speak Naam, then blesses eyes, hands, and feet when they turn toward praise, darshan, and the Lord's path. It closes with a prayer that even a sinking stone be lifted by mercy.

learnItems.title: Mercy lets the child tell the truth
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens in tenderness and dependence — the soul leans on the Lord's mercy and admits its mistakes as a child would. It then confesses how hard Hukam is to accept and ends in recognition of the Supreme Lord through the Guru.

learnItems.title: Mercy turns bitter into sweet
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens by saying the Lord already dwells in the body-fortress, even though stubbornness cannot taste Him. It travels through mercy, Guru-centered sweetness, and the hard-hearted poison of the manmukh before ending where bitter becomes sweet in Sangat.

learnItems.title: Naam planted within clears the inner fog
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens with the Perfect Guru implanting the Name and dispelling inner doubt. It travels through praise as light, ego conquered into one-pointedness, and ends where life itself depends on Naam.

learnItems.title: Nearness ends the frantic search
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens in astonished intimacy — the Lord is no longer distant but known by grace. It carries the listener through anxiety cut away, pain and pleasure losing their tyranny, and ends with essence merging into Essence.

learnItems.title: Offering everything to the One who can unite you
learnItems.summary: This shabad begins by giving up private bargaining and asking to be brought near to the Divine. It closes with fear losing its final authority.

learnItems.title: One instant of remembrance outweighs drift
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens by contrasting a life without remembrance with a life given even one true instant of simran. It then presses the contrast hard, exposing what drift becomes without the Name and where mercy finally leads.

learnItems.title: True bankers trade in Naam
learnItems.summary: The pauree opens by saying the mind's wandering stops in the company of saints. It then names the true bankers as those whose wealth is the Name and whose patience, honor, and glory ripen from listening well.

learnItems.title: Peace comes through serving the True Guru
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by joining service, peace, and the treasure of the True Name. It deepens through self-recognition, inner light, truthfulness, and praise that returns body and soul to the Lord.

learnItems.title: Pervasiveness cures the scarcity behind comparison
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by naming the Divine in all colors and forms. It then contrasts human cycling and change with the Eternal One and comes to rest in understanding received through the Guru.

learnItems.title: Place the tired mind in the Guru's cooling shelter
learnItems.summary: This tiny shabad wastes no movement. It names the Guru as giver, cooling house, and light of the three worlds, then lands on one instruction: place the mind's trust there and peace will come.

learnItems.title: Praise breaks the illusion of mastery
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with many voices singing different dimensions of the Lord's power, gifts, beauty, knowledge, making, and unmaking. It opens the field so wide that control, ownership, and single-angle thinking start to look small.

learnItems.title: Praise melts what comparison hardens
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens with metal merging into metal and uses that image to describe praise absorbed into the Praiseworthy Lord. It carries the listener through saintly dust, true action, and the home of the self being found within.

learnItems.title: Recognize greatness by the shelter it offers
learnItems.summary: This section refuses to let greatness stay abstract. The God-conscious being is described in vast terms, then recognized by what that vastness does: helps the helpless, extends a hand, and gives the way of liberation.

learnItems.title: Release arrives where seeking kneels into service
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by declaring that release comes only through the True Name. It turns seeking toward the Guru's feet, true service, and the hidden Lord found when the True Guru is pleased.

learnItems.title: Remember the Guru with every breath
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with breath-by-breath remembrance of the Guru as life and wealth. It moves through service, the washing of ego, rescue from inner fire, and finally rests in the certainty that the Guru is powerful enough to carry the soul.

learnItems.title: Remember together, not in isolation
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by calling spiritual companions close and asking them to speak of the Lord together. It carries the listener through humility, sweet speech, and the Guru's Shabad, then ends with the True King drawing the heart into Himself.

learnItems.title: Remembrance settles the body
learnItems.summary: The piece opens with remembrance repeated until peace reaches the body and anguish begins to loosen. It broadens into praise of the One Word behind scripture and ends by longing for the company of those who truly yearn for Darshan.

learnItems.title: Restlessness reveals what the heart still loves
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with a mind that will not stay still for an instant. It turns through the Guru's gift of Naam and quiet, then exposes false aims in hearts lacking love for the Lord.

learnItems.title: Sanctuary for a mind under assault
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens with a direct cry to the Father God for rescue. It carries the listener through the five thieves attacking the being, the sanctuary of the Saadh Sangat, and ends when divine light dawns in the mind.

learnItems.title: Roaming ends where holy company cools the heart
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens in relentless searching through forests, philosophies, rituals, and yogic techniques. It turns only when mercy brings true company, and then the mind and body finally cool.

learnItems.title: Service without reward reaches the Master
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by defining the servant who lives in the Guru's household — obedient, unadvertised, and absorbed in Naam. It comes to a sharp center where selfless service without reward reaches the Lord Himself.

learnItems.title: Do not let speech carry filth
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by describing greed, falsehood, slander, and anger as degrading forms of speech and appetite. It then asks a harder question: what words actually bring honor at the Lord's Door?

learnItems.title: Why waver under a merciful Creator
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by naming the Lord's mercy twice and grounding life in His gifts. It then asks why the mortal wavers when the One who created also nourishes, protects, and cherishes every heart.

learnItems.title: Steady service begins healing long separation
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens with day-and-night service, remembrance, and sweet speech offered from sanctuary. It travels through the sorrow of separation, the need for mercy, and ends with the yearning to be united with the Lord through the Guru's feet.

learnItems.title: Stop roaming where the One is already near
learnItems.summary: The pauree begins by challenging the wandering search directly and turning the seeker inward. It then sends the heart into Saadh Sangat, where ego is torn down and peace becomes possible.

learnItems.title: Pain tells the truth comfort hides
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by reversing ordinary judgment — suffering can be medicine, while pleasure can become disease when it dulls desire for God. It then yields agency back to the Creator and widens into praise of the One whose light fills everything.

learnItems.title: Peace shows up in speech and gait
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens by exposing ritual performed from self-will as the misery of an unwanted bride. It directs the heart toward saintly company and one-pointed Naam, then shows the fruit plainly: sweet speech, humble walking, and peace within.

learnItems.title: The brave war is the one against inner ego
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens by redefining courage — the real warrior subdues the vicious ego within. It then contrasts that inward bravery with the ugliness of egotistical living and comes to rest in Naam as the difference between pain and a redeemed life.

learnItems.title: The day is shrinking; spend it well
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens with time diminishing day and night and immediately urges the mind toward the Guru. It turns the shrinking day into an argument for serving saints, earning Naam, and buying what you came here to buy.

learnItems.title: The deeper union is not found by roaming
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by naming the ordinary states the mind circles within. It then declares that the fourth state, union with the Lord, is known only through the True Guru and crossed into by devotion and service.

learnItems.title: The forgiving Lord shelters the lowly
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by praising the Lord as forgiving, merciful, and tender toward the poor and unprotected. It keeps widening that refuge until the speaker can admit smallness without despair and enter sanctuary instead of comparison.

learnItems.title: The Guru asks for more than admiration
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens with startling surrender — the body itself is sold before the Perfect Guru for the Lord's sake. It develops through lamp-like wisdom, the dispersal of doubt and fear, and the final honor of having placed one's head before the True Guru.

learnItems.title: The Guru's word raises the soul into real stature
learnItems.summary: The shabad keeps returning to what the Guru's word does from the inside — it lifts the seeker beyond self-made rank, steadies the mind, and joins the heart to the Supreme Lord. What looks like attainment from the outside is recast as what the Guru actually causes within.

learnItems.title: The heart lives by the One supporting it
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by calling God the breath of life and the support of the mind. It opens further through praise, the peace of Naam, and the journey from restless desire into Saadh Sangat and Guru's vision.

learnItems.title: The key is handed to the Guru
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens with an honest plea for the saint who can show the way to the Lord. It travels through ego's curtain, Maya's sleep, and the hidden substance within, before coming to rest in the Guru holding the key.

learnItems.title: The Lord's Bani cools what is burning
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by calling the Lord's Bani ambrosial nectar. It travels through repeated hearing, the inner burning extinguished, and the mind cooled in the Guru's presence.

learnItems.title: The powerful cannot do your inner work
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by fastening the mind to the Lord and declaring that nothing else is of real use. It then strips glamour from worldly greatness, lifts up the humble servant, and ends in work done for the Lord alone.

learnItems.title: The Shabad clears the double mind
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens with contemplation of the Guru's word and the reverence it produces. It moves into abiding in true company, casting off duality, and ending in speech and mind made truthful by love.

learnItems.title: The soul was never yours to keep
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by unsettling possessive grief — relations are named, but ownership is false. It moves through Hukam, shared dust and breath, and ends when the Guru opens the shutters of doubt.

learnItems.title: The split mind becomes one through surrender
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by naming the problem sharply — the mind is ruled by evil intellect and duality. It keeps tracing that divided life through Maya, craving, and anxious loss until peace appears only through surrender, Shabad, and Naam.

learnItems.title: The world asks for peace and forgets Naam
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by saying egotism cannot produce peace. It broadens into the world's false bargaining for comfort, then returns again and again to service, Shabad, Naam, and the Lord's Will.

learnItems.title: This is not your lasting home
learnItems.summary: The pauree begins by stripping this passing world of final status. It teaches that the way to the true dwelling is known through the Guru's Shabad, and that stable belonging is found in the company of the holy rather than in what cannot go with you.

learnItems.title: Those who serve the True Guru receive the Name
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts with service to the True Guru and refuses to separate understanding from obedience. As it deepens, complaint quiets, ego is consumed, and liberation appears as love for the Beloved.

learnItems.title: Truth before beginning, truth through time
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens by naming Truth before time, mood, or human history. It strips away silence, accumulation, and cleverness, before coming to rest in the question of how falsehood breaks: by walking in Hukam.

learnItems.title: Truth gives the heart a steadier worth
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with those who please the Lord being linked to Truth. It grows into praise, sacrifice to such people, and the state of being absorbed into the Truest of the True.

learnItems.title: Truth is meant to occupy the whole life
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by joining service to the True Guru with the cleansing of mind and body. Then it keeps widening truth until it touches food, speech, company, clothing, and shelter.

learnItems.title: What comes to pass is not outside the Doer
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with the blunt fact that past actions cannot be erased. It moves through uncertainty about outcomes and ends in a harder peace: what pleases the Divine comes to pass, and there is no other Doer.

learnItems.title: Receiving under Hukam
learnItems.summary: The shabad starts by placing all becoming, giving, and receiving in the Lord's pleasure. It opens further through separation and reunion, play and service, and ends where the Creator alone is doing all that happens.

learnItems.title: What the Beloved does, I accept
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens by yielding the argument with what the Beloved does. It moves into single-hearted reliance until even honor itself is handed back to the One who gave it.

learnItems.title: When the Shabad takes the mind in hand
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with a startling image — the mind as elephant, the Guru as goad, the Shabad as the mark that disciplines it. It carries the listener through the failure of cleverness and the growth of fearlessness, then settles in daily remembrance of the One already pervading everything.

learnItems.title: Where praise makes death keep its distance
learnItems.summary: This shabad opens inside the place where the Holy keep singing the Lord's praises. It turns the heart toward a sanctuary even fear and death do not rule.

learnItems.title: Where saving company interrupts judgment
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with the fear of inescapable judgment. It directs the heart toward the saving nearness of Saadh Sangat and remembrance.

learnItems.title: The path is known by labor and generosity
learnItems.summary: The piece opens by exposing religious pose without wisdom, labor, or integrity behind it. It comes to a clean test: the one who works for what they eat and gives some away is the one who knows the path.

learnItems.title: You are family wherever fear tries to exile me
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with intimate naming — Father, Mother, relative, brother. It moves into protection, recognition by grace, and shelter that restores honor where fear had been making the world feel hostile.

learnItems.title: A passing drama is too short for waste
learnItems.summary: This brief body should not be spent as though the drama were permanent. Let mortality pull the tongue away from gossip and back toward deeds that remain.

learnItems.title: Accept what the Beloved sends
learnItems.summary: Whatever the Friend does is received as intimate care, not as a case to dispute. Let acceptance begin with trust in the One who already knows the heart.

learnItems.title: All are already within the River of Life
learnItems.summary: All beings live within the One; there is no one apart and no second outside. Receive under the Lord's pleasure; no one stands outside the One.

learnItems.title: Let praise discipline the tongue
learnItems.summary: Ambrosial speech is not merely gentle tone; it is the tongue brought under the Lord’s praise. Let praise train the mouth before sharpness takes the room.

learnItems.title: Let religion become clean conduct
learnItems.summary: The highest religion is not a label to defend but Naam becoming a cleaner way to act.

learnItems.title: Make devotion bear its own weight
learnItems.summary: Naam and conduct are not separate rooms; the tongue that remembers must not leave the hands untouched.

learnItems.title: Ask for the saint who can show the way
learnItems.summary: Peace begins with the humility to ask for the saint who can show the way past ego's curtain.

learnItems.title: Ask holy company to hold you close
learnItems.summary: Longing becomes steadier when companions draw one another close and speak of the Beloved together.

learnItems.title: Ask the Guru before the question scatters
learnItems.summary: The shabad lets confusion speak plainly, then sends it to the True Guru instead of the crowd. The turn is not another option to sample, but accepting hukam and letting selfishness be pulled from the root.

learnItems.title: Ask to be kept by the Will
learnItems.summary: The self-willed mind wastes itself in attachment, while Nanak asks to be kept by the Lord's pleasure. Peace begins when pride becomes prayer.

learnItems.title: Tell the truth like a child under mercy
learnItems.summary: The child does not hide the mistake; it tells the truth under the Father's mercy. Let confession stay near trust, not self-defense.

learnItems.title: Be brave enough to kill the inner tyrant
learnItems.summary: Real courage subdues inner ego and lets praise redeem life. Aim courage at ego before conflict at another person.

learnItems.title: Begin under the Name before anything else
learnItems.summary: The opening places the heart under the One, Truth, and the Guru's grace. Begin there before the tired self starts inventing another way to survive.

learnItems.title: Let belonging become generous
learnItems.summary: All belong to the One who is the wealth of all. Let shared dependence make the heart less possessive and more ready to pray for everyone.

learnItems.title: Bring regret under mercy, not despair
learnItems.summary: Past actions cannot be edited away, and the future is not ours to command. Let regret become honest under Hukam instead of turning into a second punishment.

learnItems.title: Bring the shrinking day to the Guru
learnItems.summary: Life is already diminishing; the Guru is where unfinished affairs are set right. Bring the unresolved day there before it disappears.

learnItems.title: Choose what endures beyond possession
learnItems.summary: Possessions can fill the hand and still leave the soul empty. Choose the wealth Guru Nanak names: praise, truth, and Naam.

learnItems.title: Buy only what can cross the threshold
learnItems.summary: Guru Nanak asks the trader within us to choose merchandise the All-knowing Merchant can receive: praise, truth, and Naam rather than visible gain.

learnItems.title: Let Naam thin the inner dread
learnItems.summary: Naam turns profit into inward fearlessness rather than more burden. Let Naam quiet the dread beneath wanting.

learnItems.title: Trade for what crosses the final threshold
learnItems.summary: The day is full of transactions, but only truth travels with the soul. Spend attention on what Guru Nanak says can still be carried.

learnItems.title: Call courage what happens after ego kneels
learnItems.summary: Courage begins where ego kneels instead of swelling. When self-conceit forgets Naam, treat the pain as a warning.

learnItems.title: Cherish the Lord by relying on mercy
learnItems.summary: The soul loves from dependence, admitting its mistakes like a child before Father and Mother. Mercy makes truth-telling safer than self-defense.

learnItems.title: Receive the nearness you keep overlooking
learnItems.summary: The True Guru protects and cherishes the helpless child until the heart blossoms. Let longing ripen where the helpless child is still being cherished.

learnItems.title: Stand where you are cherished
learnItems.summary: The Lord cherishes the humble child and keeps that heart close. Stay humble enough to be kept close and cherished.

learnItems.title: Let longing ask the sangat for the way
learnItems.summary: The search through mind and body becomes hopeful when saintly company can point toward the Beloved.

learnItems.title: Ask the path inside holy company
learnItems.summary: The searching heart admits it needs a blessed friend to point it toward the Beloved Lord.

learnItems.title: Ask the Guru to tend the child in you
learnItems.summary: The helpless child is cherished by the Guru, and the lotus-heart opens in that water. Ask to be tended before loneliness teaches you to harden.

learnItems.title: Make room for fresh Naam to settle
learnItems.summary: Freshness does not come from more movement; it comes when the mind is joined to the True Guru and Naam abides within. Let the mind stay long enough for the newness to come from inside.

learnItems.title: Cleverness cannot walk beside you
learnItems.summary: No clever scheme lasts; only walking in Hukam does. Do not confuse control with care.

learnItems.title: Put discipline on the body
learnItems.summary: Contentment, humility, and meditation make discipline plain and believable. Wear humility as discipline the body can remember.

learnItems.title: Let contentment prove your discipline
learnItems.summary: Japji turns the visible signs of renunciation inward, into contentment, humility, meditation, mortality, purity, and trust. Let the mind wear the discipline before the body displays it.

learnItems.title: Rest where attachment cannot rule
learnItems.summary: Peace begins when refuge matters more than possession or praise. Seek sanctuary before possession writes the mood.

learnItems.title: Hold the gift without gripping it
learnItems.summary: Love is steadied by release, not possession. Let love stay tender without tightening into possession.

learnItems.title: Do not decorate the life that forgot the Beloved
learnItems.summary: A life deceived by duality cannot be beautified from the outside. Do not decorate what duality is crumbling.

learnItems.title: Do not let grief turn into ownership
learnItems.summary: The shabad honors the ache but breaks the cry of 'mine.' Grief becomes clearer when the soul is returned to Hukam, one dust, one light, one breath.

learnItems.title: Do not mistake nearness for taste
learnItems.summary: The Lord is already within the body-fortress, but stubbornness cannot taste that nearness until mercy opens the Shabad on the tongue.

learnItems.title: Do not spend a passing body on a burdened tongue
learnItems.summary: The shabad holds life beside a stage-play and shows how greed, falsehood, and gossip load the soul with weight. A passing body is too precious to spend carrying a dirty tongue.

learnItems.title: Do not spend this rare life asleep
learnItems.summary: A rare body becomes self-harm when Naam is absent from its center. Wake the soul before habit spends the life for you.

learnItems.title: Do not waste the rare chance of a human life
learnItems.summary: Great fortune has already opened the door of human life. Treat the chance as too costly to spend without remembrance.

learnItems.title: Let the Guru’s word steady the doubt
learnItems.summary: Doubt loses force when the Guru’s word is allowed to govern the mind longer than argument does. Let one trusted instruction outlast the next inner objection.

learnItems.title: Duality ruins what ego keeps defending
learnItems.summary: Ego keeps its unrest alive by loving two masters. Stop asking ego for the peace only truth can hold.

learnItems.title: Ego cannot deliver the peace it promises
learnItems.summary: Ego cannot make peace; Naam cools what self-will inflames. Take Naam before self-will turns unrest into policy.

learnItems.title: Ask who is speaking when ego sounds ordinary
learnItems.summary: The shabad calls ego a chronic illness, but does not leave the soul helpless. Its cure begins when the self-important voice is exposed before the Guru's Shabad.

learnItems.title: Start where ego is finally questioned
learnItems.summary: Guru Angad turns ego into a question instead of a private identity: where does it arise, and by what discipline does it leave? Defensiveness softens when it is examined under hukam.

learnItems.title: Take the cure, not the diagnosis
learnItems.summary: The cure for ego is not insight alone; grace makes a person practice the Guru's Shabad. The day changes when humility becomes an action before pride finishes speaking.

learnItems.title: Do not call the fever your personality
learnItems.summary: Ego may feel like personality, but the shabad calls it disease and wandering. Freedom starts when the fever of selfhood is refused as the deepest truth about you.

learnItems.title: Enter the teaching as given
learnItems.summary: Even the doorway into the teaching is received, not self-composed. Let the received opening steady you before you turn spirituality into another performance.

learnItems.title: Roaming will not put doubt out
learnItems.summary: Distance and novelty cannot do what the Guru must do. Stop roaming and let inner filth be named.

learnItems.title: Wandering will not cool this fire
learnItems.summary: The fire of doubt cools through Gurmukh steadiness, not roaming. Cool doubt by becoming Gurmukh, not by escaping.

learnItems.title: Drop the private case
learnItems.summary: True company loosens selfishness, and peace returns without inner bargaining. Let sangat end the private argument.

learnItems.title: Wandering will not quench this fire
learnItems.summary: Doubt is quenched inwardly, not by more wandering. Let the Guru's teaching extinguish the inner fire.

learnItems.title: False dealing teaches the body to lie
learnItems.summary: The shabad does not treat false profit as a private mistake; it says repeated crooked dealing makes mind and body false and leaves peace out of reach.

learnItems.title: Stand inside the care already holding you
learnItems.summary: Fear wavers because it forgets who made and sustains the life it is trying to protect. The Creator who formed you is named here as the One who will also give support.

learnItems.title: Let reverence replace the room fear built
learnItems.summary: Reverent service turns fear from a ruler into a doorway. The heart becomes like the One it serves when awe steadies it from within.

learnItems.title: Fear recedes in humble company
learnItems.summary: Meeting humble beings cuts the messenger of death down to size, and mercy settles where panic had been speaking. Let company that carries the True One steady your next breath.

learnItems.title: Fill the heart until fear finds no place
learnItems.summary: When the Lord fills the heart, the world loses its power to touch the center. Fill the heart before you start measuring what can hurt you.

learnItems.title: Practice forgiveness until fear loosens
learnItems.summary: Forgiveness, good conduct, and contentment are named as the true fast. The practice weakens the inner sickness that keeps death-fear near.

learnItems.title: Practice forgiveness until fear loses its stage
learnItems.summary: The wound loses authority when forgiveness joins conduct and contentment. Fear thins because the heart no longer has to guard its grievance.

learnItems.title: Fast from retaliation
learnItems.summary: The fearless Yogi sees the Lord among trees, home, and open places. Retaliation loses force when the One being remembered is already everywhere.

learnItems.title: Do not waste the peace forgiveness brings
learnItems.summary: Forgiveness is received before peace is sustained. The blessed heart answers mercy by protecting the joy it has been given.

learnItems.title: Stop feeding the rehearsed wound
learnItems.summary: Release becomes possible when return matters more than replay. Do not keep feeding the sentence that keeps the wound alive.

learnItems.title: Turn received peace into praise
learnItems.summary: Naam meditation turns received peace into something fruitful and peace-giving. Forgiveness does not end at relief; it ripens when praise keeps moving through the day.

learnItems.title: Let forgiveness widen the whole room
learnItems.summary: Forgiveness given by the Lord does not stay private. Its peace widens until every place around the forgiven heart has room to dwell differently.

learnItems.title: Gather love at the Guru's feet
learnItems.summary: Mind and body are gathered by fastening love to the Guru. Fasten mind and body to the Guru's feet.

learnItems.title: Give the ache a day-and-night discipline
learnItems.summary: Separation is not healed by dramatizing the ache; it is steadied by serving the Guru, remembering through the day, and speaking sweetly from sanctuary.

learnItems.title: Give the frantic mind a mantra
learnItems.summary: The mind that will not stay still receives a different center when the Guru gives the Lord's mantra. Let the Name interrupt the ten-direction scatter before it becomes another chase.

learnItems.title: Give yourself where love can be trained
learnItems.summary: Love deepens when the self is offered to the Guru without reserve. Offer the withheld self where Naam can be planted.

learnItems.title: Go where death loses its swagger
learnItems.summary: Meeting the humble lowers death's threat because mercy begins to dwell in the mind.

learnItems.title: Go where ego comes off
learnItems.summary: The sight of the saints becomes a cleansing bath where self-concern can finally come off.

learnItems.title: Go where the heart is washed clean
learnItems.summary: By the saints' grace, cleansing becomes Naam on the tongue rather than another private attempt to feel clean.

learnItems.title: Let Sangat sweeten what turned bitter
learnItems.summary: The prayer asks to meet the Holy Guru so the Shabad can be tasted, and Sangat turns bitterness sweet. Let grace move you toward company instead of another private self-review.

learnItems.title: Let grace settle what you cannot
learnItems.summary: The Perfect Guru's forgiveness is not another self-improvement task; it widens into Bani, Naam, and peace shared beyond you.

learnItems.title: Let gratitude notice what mercy already did
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins by admitting that the Lord's gifts went unrecognized. Gratitude becomes honest when it names the mercy it has been living on all along.

learnItems.title: Let pity answer the unworthy heart
learnItems.summary: The shabad does not let unworthiness become despair; it places the empty-handed self under divine pity. Gratitude returns when mercy is received without pretending it was earned.

learnItems.title: Receive before demanding more
learnItems.summary: Mercy reaches the unworthy heart and restores the sight gratitude needs. Let honest gratitude become the doorway to mercy and Naam.

learnItems.title: Guard one real instant of remembrance
learnItems.summary: One moment of true remembrance steadies more than endless drift. Guard one whole instant as if it were a long life.

learnItems.title: Do not give your mouth to the wound
learnItems.summary: Truth and praise quiet the tongue before harsh words turn into grief. Keep only the speech that can stand at God's Door.

learnItems.title: Hear the Bani until it lifts you
learnItems.summary: Repeated hearing lifts the soul beyond what one reading can do. Let repeated Bani lift you higher than novelty can.

learnItems.title: Make the heart a place for Naam
learnItems.summary: The holiest place is not elsewhere; it is the heart where Naam has been allowed to live.

learnItems.title: Let the True Shabad become your sign
learnItems.summary: When the One is known within and around you, the Guru's Word is no longer only studied. It becomes the sign you carry into the Lord's court.

learnItems.title: Let closeness answer the hidden hour
learnItems.summary: The Lord keeps the humble servant clasped to His heart and cherishes the soul like a child. Let that nearness speak louder than the silence.

learnItems.title: Honor what the Guru honors
learnItems.summary: The Guru rebukes contempt and honors woman as the doorway through which human life comes. Let truth and dignity replace contempt in speech and conduct.

learnItems.title: Honor the one through whom you arrived
learnItems.summary: The one through whom life arrives cannot be spoken of with contempt. Do not diminish the one the Guru honors.

learnItems.title: Refuse contempt at its source
learnItems.summary: Guru Nanak answers contempt with reality: human life, friendship, lineage, and kings themselves come through woman.

learnItems.title: Nothing stands outside Hukam
learnItems.summary: All conditions unfold within Hukam, and ego shrinks when this is understood. Stop searching for a place outside Hukam.

learnItems.title: See everything standing inside Hukam
learnItems.summary: Bodies, souls, status, pain, blessing, and wandering all stand inside Hukam. Let that wideness leave ego with less to say.

learnItems.title: Begin within Hukam
learnItems.summary: Bodies, souls, pain, blessing, wandering, and greatness all stand inside Hukam. Understanding this leaves ego with less to announce and less to defend.

learnItems.title: Treat this human birth as an invitation
learnItems.summary: The verse does not flatter the body; it gives it a purpose. Spend today as someone invited to meet the Lord while breath is still here.

learnItems.title: Do not spend a rare life like loose change
learnItems.summary: The shabad names the crossing and the waste in the same breath. Effort belongs to the way across; Maya turns the life sideways.

learnItems.title: Do not waste the crossing
learnItems.summary: This life is given for crossing and meeting, not decoration. Treat this life as opportunity, not drift.

learnItems.title: Learn love from those who live it
learnItems.summary: Spiritual companions teach love by drawing close and telling the stories of the all-powerful Beloved.

learnItems.title: Learning is empty when Maya is still loved
learnItems.summary: Religious learning stays hollow while attachment still rules the heart. Let learning bow to the God it claims to know.

learnItems.title: Stay near the Perfect Guru, not another portion
learnItems.summary: The Creator is already near, and the True Guru is perfect. Envy loosens when the heart returns to the duty and grace actually given.

learnItems.title: Serve before complaint takes the mouth
learnItems.summary: Serving the True Guru receives Naam into the mind until peace outlasts the urge to protest.

learnItems.title: Let devotion quiet the wandering appetite
learnItems.summary: Devotion brings bliss and lets the wandering mind rest at the Lord's feet. When restlessness wants novelty, stay where devotion is already becoming sweet.

learnItems.title: Let fresh Naam settle inside
learnItems.summary: Naam enters the mind as an ever-fresh inward renewal. Let the Name refresh the place that distraction keeps trying to entertain.

learnItems.title: Let holy company lift Maya's dust
learnItems.summary: The True Guru gives support to every soul, so company is not escape; it is where love learns to lean on the One who already holds it.

learnItems.title: Let hope outrank the world's reach
learnItems.summary: Hope in the Lord outranks the reach of the world. Let the Guru-revealed Lord outrank the world's reach.

learnItems.title: Let Naam swallow the smaller fears
learnItems.summary: Naam absorbs the heart until the lesser fears no longer hold the room. Let the nectar of the Unspoken become larger than the alarm.

learnItems.title: Let nearness end the split vision
learnItems.summary: Grace makes the Lord near enough to be seen everywhere. Let trust return before inquiry multiplies again.

learnItems.title: Let praise become the place you live
learnItems.summary: Peace deepens when praise, service, and Shabad replace self-importance. Serve and let praise house the heart.

learnItems.title: Let praise dye the whole life true
learnItems.summary: Praise is not decoration; it dyes the self with truthful color until action begins to carry that hue.

learnItems.title: Let praise loosen your need to grasp
learnItems.summary: The Lord's power and gifts are sung, not controlled. Praise opens the clenched hand by returning it to wonder.

learnItems.title: Let protection become felt, not recited
learnItems.summary: The shabad names the Lord as Father, Mother, relative, and brother until protection becomes intimate. Let shelter become personal enough to be trusted.

learnItems.title: Let seeking kneel into service
learnItems.summary: The saints are told that release comes through the True Name, and the Guru's feet become the real pilgrimage. Seeking matures when it stops shopping for rescue and begins serving where the Name has already opened the way.

learnItems.title: Let seeking kneel before it wanders
learnItems.summary: Release is found where Naam and service meet the Guru. Bring the question near a line you can actually keep.

learnItems.title: Let service become the way across
learnItems.summary: Service bears fruit when the Guru brings it into the Lord’s pleasure. Let today’s work become remembrance, not self-display.

learnItems.title: Let service make room for the Lord
learnItems.summary: Service becomes clean when it lets the Lord dwell within and keeps filth from sticking. Let service purify the body before image enters the room.

learnItems.title: Let service make your life weighty
learnItems.summary: Service becomes fruitful when the whole life is offered through it. Make the day's next task fruitful through Naam.

learnItems.title: Hand your honor back to the Master
learnItems.summary: The servant does not have to manufacture dignity in every room. Nanak places honor and greatness in the Master’s hands, where pride can stop arguing for itself.

learnItems.title: Let shelter be personal again
learnItems.summary: The prayer names the Lord as Father, Mother, kin, and brother before fear can make the soul feel orphaned. Shelter becomes believable because it is intimate.

learnItems.title: Let the Bani cool what is burning
learnItems.summary: The Lord's Bani cools the heart like nectar taken in again. Let repeated hearing answer the inner fire before another reaction speaks for you.

learnItems.title: Let the Beloved's way please you
learnItems.summary: The shabad does not merely endure the Friend's actions; it lets them become pleasing. Consent deepens when the heart stops treating the Beloved's way as a wound.

learnItems.title: Let the body learn surrender first
learnItems.summary: Devotion becomes real when the body enters surrender. Let surrender reach the body before speech negotiates.

learnItems.title: Let the Court name the honor
learnItems.summary: Those who meet the Guru in loving faith are accepted, and the True One gives them a place in the Lord's Court. Let love-filled attunement matter more than visible credit.

learnItems.title: Let the deeper fear swallow the lesser ones
learnItems.summary: Naam absorbs the heart so deeply that lesser fears are forgotten. Let reverence and taste become larger than the anxieties asking to govern you.

learnItems.title: Let the filled heart leave doubt behind
learnItems.summary: A heart filled with the Lord is made whole, and doubt falls away. Fill the heart with the Lord until doubt has nowhere to stand.

learnItems.title: Let the Guru's goad train the wild mind
learnItems.summary: The Guru's Shabad trains the wild mind and guards the inner treasure. Let the Shabad's goad interrupt clever impulse.

learnItems.title: Let the Guru's way outrank the powerful
learnItems.summary: The Guru's way outweighs millions of worldly rewards. Do not let worldly power outrank the Guru's path.

learnItems.title: Let the Guru's word lift you into real stature
learnItems.summary: The Guru's word lifts the soul into true stature. Let the Guru's word, not your image, define stature.

learnItems.title: Let the Guru's word rein the mind
learnItems.summary: The mind is an elephant until the Guru's Shabad becomes its true mark and rein. Trust begins when cleverness stops pretending to govern the soul.

learnItems.title: Let Naam answer the ache of incompletion
learnItems.summary: The shabad answers lack by placing Naam in the heart — the path, cleansing, and honor become whole under the Perfect One's shelter.

learnItems.title: Let the mind lean where life comes from
learnItems.summary: The Lord is the mind's support and the soul's breath; praise teaches the heart where to rest.

learnItems.title: Let the Name clear the fog
learnItems.summary: The Guru plants Naam so doubt gives way to light and direction. Let planted Naam become the light for the next step.

learnItems.title: Let Naam make the heart whole before anyone approves
learnItems.summary: The shabad repeats “perfect” until wholeness is relocated from circumstance into the heart where Naam lives. Standing is safest when completeness is received there first.

learnItems.title: Let the scheme die before it runs you
learnItems.summary: Ego loosens when faith in the Guru outlives frantic schemes. Let one protective scheme die under the Guru's care.

learnItems.title: Let the Shabad lead doubt into Sangat
learnItems.summary: The Guru's Word fills the heart with reverence and keeps it joined to the True Congregation. Doubt begins to clear when remembrance stops being private noise and becomes shared praise.

learnItems.title: Let the divided mind become one act
learnItems.summary: The mind under duality stays unfinished until it surrenders through the Guru. Begin where the split is loudest, and let one guided act gather the heart back into One.

learnItems.title: Let Truth be seen before feedback arrives
learnItems.summary: The shabad steadies the heart by widening its sight — those attuned to Truth see the True One everywhere. Worth stops shrinking when the room is no longer the largest reality.

learnItems.title: Let vastness loosen your grip
learnItems.summary: The same One is sung as power, gift, beauty, distance, and nearness. Vastness loosens the grip by making one angle too small to rule the whole.

learnItems.title: Let wandering end where the Guru leads
learnItems.summary: The deeper state is not reached by roaming through moods, methods, or explanations. The shabad names the crossing plainly: devotion to the Lord and service to the Guru carry the soul beyond its circling.

learnItems.title: Let the heart be dyed in what cannot flatter you
learnItems.summary: Truth does not flatter the ego; it dyes the heart until worth is absorbed into what is real. This is dignity without performance, received by meditation rather than borrowed from applause.

learnItems.title: Receive the life the Guru gives
learnItems.summary: The True Guru plants the Lord in the heart and grants the life of the soul through the Ambrosial Naam. Let worth begin with received life, not self-measurement.

learnItems.title: Measure greatness by the Life the Guru plants within
learnItems.summary: The shabad measures greatness by gift — meeting the True Guru enshrines the Lord in the heart, and the Perfect Guru grants the life of the soul. Dignity begins as received life, not public size.

learnItems.title: Make the hands good by what they serve
learnItems.summary: The shabad blesses hands when they write praise and feet when they walk the Lord’s way.

learnItems.title: Measure greatness by what the heart clings to
learnItems.summary: True greatness is loving attachment to the Lord, not to Maya's scale. Measure greatness by freedom from anxious status.

learnItems.title: Meet the True One before you brace
learnItems.summary: The heart is saved as ego is subdued and hostile energies are made to serve. Put faith in the True Guru before self-protection becomes another scheme.

learnItems.title: Melt the self into praise
learnItems.summary: Praise is not self-improvement; it is metal returning to metal, the separate self taking on the deep crimson color of Truth.

learnItems.title: Mercy brings the Name home
learnItems.summary: Bliss, poise, and the Name are not conquered by self-improvement. When the Master is merciful, Naam comes home to the mind.

learnItems.title: Open the hand for the jewel mercy gives
learnItems.summary: The Jewel of Naam is not seized by force; it is given by mercy and held in the Guru-facing life. Practice receiving before the self-willed grip loses what it wanted to control.

learnItems.title: Taste the sweetness hidden in the fortress
learnItems.summary: The Lord is already within the body-fortress, but stubbornness cannot taste Him. Mercy opens the Guru's Shabad until nearness becomes something the heart can actually taste.

learnItems.title: Win the inner field first
learnItems.summary: Conquering the mind matters more than conquering the world around you. Conquer the mind where the world first enters.

learnItems.title: Make room for the Name by wanting less
learnItems.summary: The body can name a hundred pleasures, but Naam needs room in the heart. Let one desired thing remain unchosen so remembrance has somewhere to dwell.

learnItems.title: Name the house duality built
learnItems.summary: Duality builds a whole inner house for ego to inhabit. Name duality before it furnishes the mind.

learnItems.title: Clasp praise closer than craving
learnItems.summary: The shabad contrasts the begging hand of desire with the Gurmukh who keeps the Lord's praise clasped to the heart. Choose nearness over the urge to acquire and be noticed.

learnItems.title: Let the Shabad pierce the false shelter
learnItems.summary: The soul-bride is not made secure by polish or hiding; beauty begins when the Shabad breaks through the false self.

learnItems.title: Notice how appetite grows
learnItems.summary: Craving does not arrive fully grown; the shabad notices its first attachments before they harden into direction. Catch the small want while it is still teachable.

learnItems.title: Keep command and Naam in one breath
learnItems.summary: The Guru's command is kept truly when obedience carries Naam inside it. Keep the command with Naam inside it.

learnItems.title: Keep one repetition until it changes you
learnItems.summary: Naam deepens when one return is kept past mood and vanity. Stay with one-pointed Naam until the walk becomes pure.

learnItems.title: One remembered instant outweighs filth
learnItems.summary: One clean instant of remembrance outweighs a filthy habit. Trust one clean instant to break an old habit.

learnItems.title: Ownership fails at the first question
learnItems.summary: The first questions of grief already loosen the claim of ownership. Let grief loosen the ownership it cannot keep.

learnItems.title: Receive the cooling that effort could not earn
learnItems.summary: After all the searching and technique, patience arrives as mercy: holy company cools the body, settles the mind, and makes room for joy.

learnItems.title: Let listening become your wealth
learnItems.summary: Patience, glory, and honor gather around the one who keeps listening to the Name, making delay a place of inward trade rather than resentment.

learnItems.title: Let mercy stop the mind's roaming
learnItems.summary: The wandering mind does not become patient by scolding itself; it steadies when mercy places it in saintly company and light enters.

learnItems.title: Let patience gather real wealth
learnItems.summary: In holy company, wandering stops and patience ripens into Naam-rich honor. Wait by listening instead of simmering.

learnItems.title: Peace comes by serving, not starring
learnItems.summary: Serving the Guru brings peace and exposes the self to light. Serve quietly until the Lord's light exposes the self.

learnItems.title: Piling up will not satisfy hunger
learnItems.summary: The opening of Japji Sahib sets Truth before every age, then exposes how accumulation cannot feed the soul. Let what is forever true measure what you are trying to add.

learnItems.title: Let praise and insult lose their claim
learnItems.summary: Freedom begins when praise and slander stop moving the center. Let praise and insult pass through the same door.

learnItems.title: Do not trade the jewel-mind for doubt
learnItems.summary: The mind is called a priceless jewel, not a debating room to be spent cheaply. Place it in Naam and sangat before doubt bargains away its honor.

learnItems.title: Spend the day on profit that remains
learnItems.summary: Real profit is not accumulation; it is the heart returning to Naam, service, and truth while breath is still here.

learnItems.title: Pure conduct outranks spiritual display.
learnItems.summary: The highest religion is the Lord's Name, pure conduct, and the cleansing of the mind in holy company. Let the Lord's Name and pure conduct remain one.

learnItems.title: Put your hope where the world cannot reach
learnItems.summary: The heart filled with the Lord is not ruled by the world's pressure. Let hope rise above the reach of what can stain, threaten, or demand your center.

learnItems.title: Receive the belonging you did not manufacture
learnItems.summary: Belonging is received from the One who already holds everyone. Receive belonging from the One, not from self-defense.

learnItems.title: Recognize the One within before you teach
learnItems.summary: Knowledge ripens only when the One is recognized within. Say the cleaner thing and keep it.

learnItems.title: Let remembrance outrun the spiral
learnItems.summary: The shabad repeats remembrance until peace becomes more than an idea. Simran gives the spiraling mind one holy word to return to before imagined danger takes command.

learnItems.title: Remember until worry leaves the body
learnItems.summary: Repeated remembrance brings peace close enough for worry and anguish to loosen from the body.

learnItems.title: Let simran cool the body from within
learnItems.summary: This passage does not treat worry as only mental; it says remembrance dispels anguish from the body. Naam is allowed to reach the chest, shoulders, and breath where fear has settled.

learnItems.title: Rest in the nearness already given
learnItems.summary: Grace makes the Beloved known as intimate, not distant. Let the chase quiet when the True Guru points to the One already near.

learnItems.title: Rest the mind on what already carries it
learnItems.summary: God is named as the breath of the soul and the support of the mind. Rest begins when praise answers that support instead of the mind pretending to carry itself.

learnItems.title: Restless hearts also need love
learnItems.summary: Restlessness deepens when the heart lacks love for the Lord. Let that love gather the mind before the next distraction gets a vote.

learnItems.title: Run to sanctuary before fear hardens
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with an unguarded cry — save me, Father; all virtues are Yours. Fear softens when it reaches sanctuary before it builds a self-protective shell.

learnItems.title: Stay where the heart is helped
learnItems.summary: This rare human life is meant to join holy company, meditate on Naam, and make the effort to cross.

learnItems.title: Scarcity breaks in a world already pervaded
learnItems.summary: The One pervades every color and form, while the measuring mind keeps circling through lack. Comparison weakens when fullness is seen before rank.

learnItems.title: Let searching speak its real hunger
learnItems.summary: Searching clears when it admits hunger for Darshan and stops roaming alone. Bring that hunger into company instead of making another private plan.

learnItems.title: Stop roaming for what saintly company gives
learnItems.summary: Restless searching settles when saintly company cools the mind and body. let seeking kneel into saintly company.

learnItems.title: Let holy company cool the body
learnItems.summary: Holy company cools the body before the mind can settle. Take the agitation where patient remembrance can reach the breath first.

learnItems.title: Let the search cool in saintly company
learnItems.summary: The shabad names the exhaustion of forests, philosophies, rituals, postures, and repeated rising without peace. Let the search cool where mercy brings holy company.

learnItems.title: Seek the humble servant, not the impressive name
learnItems.summary: The humble servant carries more help than the impressive name. Choose the blessed servant over the impressive name.

learnItems.title: Do not envy greatness that is sick with worry
learnItems.summary: Those who appear powerful still carry the disease of anxiety. The shabad frees the heart from craving a stature that cannot give peace.

learnItems.title: Serve without making yourself the headline
learnItems.summary: Service becomes pure when the self stops asking to be noticed. Keep service hidden enough for Naam to stay central.

learnItems.title: Do the work without pricing it
learnItems.summary: Reward-seeking empties service before the work is even done. Finish the work before ego sends its invoice.

learnItems.title: Serve without auditioning for reward
learnItems.summary: Selfless service reaches the Lord when reward is no longer the motive. Serve without reward so the affair can be resolved.

learnItems.title: Let service stay hidden and real
learnItems.summary: Service becomes true when the self stops asking to be seen. Let hidden service leave the self unseen, quieter, and true.

learnItems.title: Serve until mind and body agree
learnItems.summary: Service to the True Guru does not cleanse intention alone; it makes mind and body answer to the same truth.

learnItems.title: Serve until separation starts healing
learnItems.summary: Longing is not healed by dramatizing distance; the shabad places it inside day-and-night service, remembrance, sanctuary, and sweet speech. Separation begins to soften when the self is renounced at the Guru's threshold.

learnItems.title: Let service quiet the complaint
learnItems.summary: Serving the True Guru receives Naam until peace has somewhere to live and complaint loses its claim on the mouth.

learnItems.title: Serve with one gathered awareness
learnItems.summary: Service becomes true when love is gathered toward the One. Gather love into the Lord's Will before calling it service.

learnItems.title: Service carries the seeker across
learnItems.summary: The fourth state is not reached by more roaming; the True Guru makes union known. Devotion and Guru-service become the crossing the restless seeker could not invent.

learnItems.title: Keep peace alive with Bani
learnItems.summary: The Perfect Guru gives rare peace by grace, and Bani keeps it sounding. Singing the Word makes forgiveness fruitful instead of fragile.

learnItems.title: Sing until doubt loses its room
learnItems.summary: Sung Naam turns inner light on and shows the way. Sing the Name until the way is visible.

learnItems.title: Speak what can stand accepted at the Door
learnItems.summary: Guru Nanak names speech by its destination: words that bring honor are accepted, while harsh words leave the foolish mind grieving. The test of speech is whether it can stand before the Beloved.

learnItems.title: Refuse to feed the mouth with slander’s filth
learnItems.summary: The shabad uses startling images for corrupt speech — greed as a dog, falsehood as filth, slander as another person’s dirt placed in your own mouth. The mouth is protected by refusing that meal.

learnItems.title: Do not let anger set the mouth on fire
learnItems.summary: The same shabad names anger as the cremation-ground fire that burns through speech. Honor begins when the mouth refuses to become the place where resentment disposes of others.

learnItems.title: Spend the remaining day on what lasts
learnItems.summary: Day and night are reducing the account. Spend the remaining hours on the profit of Naam instead of another postponement.

learnItems.title: Stand where fear cannot rule
learnItems.summary: The thieves are conquered and the mind fills with divine light. Stand where illumination, not threat, gets to rule your speech and body.

learnItems.title: Stay awake over what the Guru has given
learnItems.summary: Ask the Guru, then stay awake enough to guard what has been entrusted. Ask the Guru, then protect the answer.

learnItems.title: Go where selfishness can soften
learnItems.summary: True congregation leads the heart to the Lord, loosens selfishness, and lets peace merge like water in water.

learnItems.title: Let mercy stop the wavering
learnItems.summary: The Lord Master is merciful before the mind has managed to settle. Let the repeated mercy of the Creator steady the place that keeps wavering.

learnItems.title: Stop wavering where mercy already holds you
learnItems.summary: The shabad begins with mercy before it confronts fear. Wavering loses authority when the heart hears, again and again, that the Lord Master is merciful.

learnItems.title: Accept the difficult sweetness of Hukam
learnItems.summary: This source admits that speaking is easy while accepting Hukam is difficult. Tell the truth like a child, then practice receiving the Will you cannot manage.

learnItems.title: Stop arguing with what is already under Hukam
learnItems.summary: Past actions cannot be rewritten, and tomorrow is not in the ego's possession. Mercy begins when regret stops prosecuting what the Doer already holds.

learnItems.title: When status is useless, choose the servant path
learnItems.summary: The powerful people of the world cannot do the soul’s work. The shabad turns comparison away from impressive names and toward humble usefulness before the Lord.

learnItems.title: Stop exhausting yourself before prayer
learnItems.summary: The prayer begins where self-rescue has run out — Save me, Father; all virtues are Yours. Let helplessness become honest prayer instead of another performance.

learnItems.title: Stop measuring forms the One already fills
learnItems.summary: Every color and form is pervaded by the Divine, while the restless mind keeps circling. Comparison fades when the heart stops measuring inside a filled world.

learnItems.title: Stop waiting for a better time
learnItems.summary: The shabad refuses the mind that keeps searching the calendar for devotion. Start before the next excuse becomes your teacher.

learnItems.title: Stop waiting for the right time
learnItems.summary: The right time appears only when remembrance begins now. Begin now before planning becomes another delay.

learnItems.title: Stubbornness is not a spiritual path
