learnItems.summary: The shabad refuses the fantasy that force of will can discover the One. Fruitful service happens when the Lord draws the seeker near, so the honest posture is surrender rather than spiritual self-assertion.

learnItems.title: Let pain teach what comfort keeps hiding
learnItems.summary: Pain becomes medicine when it uncovers what comfort hides. Let pain uncover dependence comfort concealed.

learnItems.title: Let helplessness tell the truth
learnItems.summary: Pain can wake dependence when pleasure has kept the heart asleep. Let the limit tell the truth, then answer it with praise of the One whose light fills everything.

learnItems.title: Let pain widen into the One Light
learnItems.summary: The wound opens into wonder as the One whose limits cannot be known shines through every creature.

learnItems.title: Let pain uncover what comfort was hiding
learnItems.summary: Pain can uncover the dependence comfort often keeps hidden. Let pain tell the truth before comfort edits it.

learnItems.title: Let sangat make peace audible in your tone
learnItems.summary: The shabad joins holy company, Naam, and peace until remembrance reaches the sound of a person’s life. Speech becomes sweet because the heart has stayed near the saints and kept the Beloved within.

learnItems.title: Let the Guru’s Will empty the ego from speech
learnItems.summary: Here sweetness comes through the Guru’s Will: the nectar is received with ease, and those who drink it lose ego from within. Speech grows gentle because the self no longer needs to occupy every word.

learnItems.title: Let remembrance soften the walk
learnItems.summary: Here sweetness of speech is the fruit of sangat, one-pointed Naam, and humility in the body. Let remembrance reach the tone, the pace, and the way you enter the room.

learnItems.title: Take envy to the feet that wash the heart
learnItems.summary: The one blessed with complete grace touches the feet of the Holy. Comparison is not argued away; it is washed in sangat, humility, and Naam.

learnItems.title: Take the crowded body into saintly company
learnItems.summary: Meeting the Holy Saint breaks lust and anger in the crowded body. Return the breath before the wound chooses the tone.

learnItems.title: Take your doubt to saintly company
learnItems.summary: Doubt clears when it seeks living guidance instead of circling alone. Bring doubt to the saint who can pierce ego's curtain.

learnItems.title: The battlefield changes when the Guru is with you
learnItems.summary: Praise cools the mind, and the Perfect Guru turns the arduous field into a place of victory. Fear changes when the battle is no longer fought alone.

learnItems.title: The brave fight is inward
learnItems.summary: True courage subdues the vicious ego within, not another person. Win the inward war by praising Naam.

learnItems.title: Return agency to the Creator
learnItems.summary: Pain becomes medicine when it exposes the false claim that the self is in charge. Return agency to the Creator whose light and work pervade everything.

learnItems.title: True action finds the inward door
learnItems.summary: The inward door opens as other hopes are abandoned for the One Shabad. True action begins by helping the gaze turn toward the One.

learnItems.title: Trade in Naam, not passing profit
learnItems.summary: True wealth is earned in Naam and ripens through patient living. Let truthful steadiness outrun self-protection.

learnItems.title: Trust the cooling house
learnItems.summary: The Guru is cooling shelter, light, and lasting wealth for a tired mind. Place trust there before another temporary fix asks to become your refuge.

learnItems.title: Truth was here before your urgency
learnItems.summary: Truth stands before beginning, through time, and beyond this heated moment. Urgency loses authority when it is measured against what was already true.

learnItems.title: Turn back before distance hardens into pain
learnItems.summary: The prayer becomes poor, meek, and direct — save me, because I am Yours. Naam is not decoration here; it is the support that keeps distance from hardening into another wound.

learnItems.title: Use your hands for praise, not stain
learnItems.summary: Hands are called good when they become instruments of praise rather than tools of impulse or vanity.

learnItems.title: Let the running mind dwell in Sangat
learnItems.summary: The pauree names the cure for mental wandering as dwelling with the saints, where mercy enlightens the mind. The search becomes home when company, patience, and Naam replace the habit of running after the next voice.

learnItems.title: Watch appetite grow before it rules you
learnItems.summary: The shabad gives appetite a biography, beginning with innocent dependence and warning how desire keeps taking new names. Watch the want before it learns to speak as you.

learnItems.title: Receive what is given under Hukam
learnItems.summary: What pleases the Lord comes to pass, and what is given is what we receive. The daily practice is not control, but clean receiving under the True Creator.

learnItems.title: Receive what is given and keep the Naam
learnItems.summary: The Lord gives, and mercy turns receiving into the Jewel of Naam. Unchosen circumstances become less barren when the hand reaches for remembrance.

learnItems.title: Receive reunion without forgetting the Doer
learnItems.summary: Separation and reunion both move within the Creator's doing. When closeness returns, the soul receives it as grace instead of turning reunion into possession.

learnItems.title: Receive what the Beloved gives
learnItems.summary: Whatever pleases the Beloved comes to pass, and what is given is what the soul receives. Receive the moment under the One who gives, separates, and reunites.

learnItems.title: Ask the way before appetite answers
learnItems.summary: After tracing craving through a whole life, the shabad ends without sentiment: without the Guru, the world is drowning. The soul needs direction before desire turns another impulse into a road.

learnItems.title: Without the Beloved, decoration stays hollow
learnItems.summary: Without the Beloved, decoration cannot cover a heart split by duality. Do not ask decoration to cover duality.

learnItems.title: Without the Beloved, even one instant burns
learnItems.summary: Without the Beloved, the ache beneath doubt is exposed. Stay with Shabad until aching separation tells the truth.

learnItems.title: Earn cleanly and keep the hand open
learnItems.summary: Honest labor and open-handed giving reveal a truer path. Let honest earning become open-handed knowing.

learnItems.title: Do not bow to performative holiness
learnItems.summary: Guru Nanak strips status from religious pose and gives the path a harder test: honest work and a hand that shares.

learnItems.title: Do not bow to borrowed authority
learnItems.summary: The shabad refuses reverence for a teacher whose status depends on begging and display. Let discernment look for honest work before it bows.

learnItems.title: Earn honestly and let some leave your hand
learnItems.summary: The path is known in honest earning and open-handed giving. Refuse spiritual status that feeds on begging.

learnItems.title: Give thanks for the meeting that broke the inner crowd
learnItems.summary: The body-village crowded by desire and anger is broken open by meeting the Holy Saint. Your turning toward the Guru is already grace at work, not evidence of your private strength.

learnItems.title: When heat reaches the tongue
learnItems.summary: Begin under Truth that was here before the flare-up, then let Hukam make the next sentence smaller, slower, and less owned by heat.

learnItems.title: Anger under the Truth that Outlasts It
learnItems.summary: Begin with Truth that stands before and beyond the flare-up. This path lets anger lose its claim to be final, then walks the tongue back toward Hukam, truthful speech, and steadier service.

learnItems.title: When anger starts keeping score
learnItems.summary: Begin with Truth that stands before every injury. These readings help anger stop building a courtroom out of comparison.

learnItems.title: When anger borrows discipline’s clothes
learnItems.summary: Hold anger under the Mool Mantar until discipline can be separated from the need to punish, control, or sound righteous.

learnItems.title: When the body starts to waver
learnItems.summary: Start with the question Guru Arjan asks the trembling heart: why waver when the One who made you still gives support?

learnItems.title: Anxiety held by the Creator
learnItems.summary: Start with the question the shabad asks the wavering heart: why shake when the One who made you still gives support? The readings move fear from private weather into remembered care, Hukam, and prayerful dependence.

learnItems.title: When fear hardens into anger
learnItems.summary: Start with the Merciful Creator who nourishes what He creates. These readings cool anxiety before it recruits anger as armor.

learnItems.title: When worry must be interrupted by mercy
learnItems.summary: These readings pull anxiety away from imagined loss and make it count the mercies already carrying the day.

learnItems.title: When praise and blame start pulling you
learnItems.summary: Rest in the Lord’s sanctuary until praise, slander, pleasure, and pain lose the authority to drag the heart around.

learnItems.title: Attachment without the chain
learnItems.summary: Begin where praise and slander, pleasure and pain have too much authority. This path loosens attachment without making the heart cold, returning desire to the Guru until love can stay tender and free.

learnItems.title: When clinging builds a throne
learnItems.summary: The shabad equalizes pleasure and pain, gold and copper, praise and slander. This path lets attachment lose the power to crown the self.

learnItems.title: When clinging starts speaking for you
learnItems.summary: These readings slow the tongue before attachment turns desire into pressure, bargaining, or command.

learnItems.title: When comparison hardens the eye
learnItems.summary: Let the image of metal merging with metal interrupt the separate self that keeps ranking, then return the eye to praise, true action, and homecoming.

learnItems.title: Comparison melted into praise
learnItems.summary: Start with the shabad's image of metal merging with metal and praise absorbed into the Praiseworthy One. These readings lead envy away from ranking and toward saintly company, true action, and the crimson color of Truth.

learnItems.title: When comparison exiles the heart
learnItems.summary: Begin with praise melting into the Praiseworthy One. These readings return the comparing heart to shared devotion before envy becomes exile.

learnItems.title: When envy needs useful hands
learnItems.summary: These readings interrupt comparison by sending its restless energy into seva, where another person’s need becomes more important than your rank.

learnItems.title: Let conduct stand behind the mouth
learnItems.summary: These readings keep speech beside conduct until the tongue stops seeking exemption from the heart’s condition.

learnItems.title: When control tightens the room
learnItems.summary: Let the many songs of Jap widen the room until management looks too small and praise becomes the honest response to what you cannot command.

learnItems.title: Control undone by vast praise
learnItems.summary: Begin among the many voices singing divine power, gifts, beauty, and command. The path widens the mind until control looks too small for reality and action can become obedient rather than possessive.

learnItems.title: When control sends the body its bill
learnItems.summary: The shabad opens the field of divine power, gifts, making, and unmaking until control looks too small to carry the world.

learnItems.title: Release the hand without abandoning the task
learnItems.summary: Begin where the Lord’s pleasure governs giving and receiving. These readings teach action that is obedient without pretending to author the outcome.

learnItems.title: When discipline turns inward first
learnItems.summary: A three-step bundle for the moment discipline starts looking outward for something to control. It returns the work to contentment, brotherhood, and the bowed mind that can be governed from within.

learnItems.title: Discipline that bows before it conquers
learnItems.summary: Move from outward rigor into the harder discipline Guru Nanak names: contentment, humility, shared belonging, and the mind conquered before the world is judged.

learnItems.title: When discipline has gone hard around pain
learnItems.summary: These readings let inward discipline meet forgiveness before principle becomes punishment wearing a sacred name.

learnItems.title: When discipline becomes useful to someone else
learnItems.summary: These readings move discipline beyond self-improvement and spend practiced strength on a burden that can actually be lightened.

learnItems.title: When doubt keeps circling the fire
learnItems.summary: A three-step bundle for the hour when second-guessing is feeding its own heat. It brings the mind from wandering argument into the Guru-word that kills ego and thirst at the root.

learnItems.title: When doubt is cooled by the Guru’s word
learnItems.summary: Follow doubt out of roaming and into the Guru’s teaching, where the mind receives words strong enough to kill ego’s thirst and cool the inner blaze.

learnItems.title: Let the Guru’s word outlast the fog
learnItems.summary: Stay near the Guru’s word and saintly company until wandering loses its authority and clarity becomes a practiced dwelling.

learnItems.title: Take the question into better company
learnItems.summary: These readings move the question from isolation into sangat, where peace has a living witness and the mind no longer argues alone.

learnItems.title: When uncertainty reaches the tongue
learnItems.summary: These readings slow the mouth before doubt turns into needless suspicion, complaint, or confusion handed to others.

learnItems.title: When the self fills the room
learnItems.summary: A three-step bundle for the moment self-importance starts naming reality for everyone else. It treats ego as a chronic disease and turns the body back toward the Shabad that grace makes possible.

learnItems.title: The cure hidden inside ego’s illness
learnItems.summary: Begin with Guru Angad’s unsparing diagnosis of ego as a chronic disease, then follow the cure that appears through grace and lived obedience to the Guru’s Shabad.

learnItems.title: Let gratitude break the self open
learnItems.summary: The shabad names ego as disease and grace as cure. These readings let gratitude expose what self-importance cannot heal.

learnItems.title: Let the self step down from the center
learnItems.summary: Walk through the diagnosis of haumai until humility becomes less like self-hatred and more like receiving the cure.

learnItems.title: When waiting exposes the ego
learnItems.summary: These readings let delay reveal the ego’s demand to be served now, then teach the heart to wait under grace instead.

learnItems.title: When exhaustion needs a true beginning
learnItems.summary: A three-step bundle for the hour when strength is too thin to perform. It lets the opening truth of Ik Oankar, Sat Naam, and Guru’s grace become the first ground beneath the tired mind.

learnItems.title: Begin the tired day under Ik Oankar
learnItems.summary: Let the journey start where the cited shabad starts: not with more force, but with Ik Oankar, Truth, the Creator’s presence, and the Guru’s grace before any next step is demanded.

learnItems.title: When fear feels like exile
learnItems.summary: A three-step bundle for the hour when fear makes the world feel hostile and the body feel alone. It returns to the shabad’s intimate names — Father, Mother, relative, brother — until shelter becomes personal again.

learnItems.title: When fear is answered by kinship with the One
learnItems.summary: Move from fear’s exile into the shabad’s intimate names for God: Father, Mother, relative, brother, protector, and shelter close enough to restore courage.

learnItems.title: When one fear becomes the climate
learnItems.summary: The shabad answers exile by naming divine kinship as Father, Mother, relative, brother, and shelter. These readings keep fear from becoming the whole atmosphere.

learnItems.title: Let vigilance become trust
learnItems.summary: These readings do not shame vigilance; they place it under the Merciful Creator until protection is no longer confused with constant bracing.

learnItems.title: When forgiveness learns fearlessness
learnItems.summary: A short bundle for opening the old grip without pretending the wound was small. It follows forgiveness into the Presence already within and outside the house, where fear loses its argument.

learnItems.title: Forgiveness that becomes fearlessness
learnItems.summary: Follow forgiveness from received mercy into courage, so the heart can stop guarding the wound as if bitterness were protection.

learnItems.title: When release becomes another appetite
learnItems.summary: These readings guard forgiveness from becoming a new form of bargaining, credit, or moral ownership.

learnItems.title: Enoughness learned through gratitude
learnItems.summary: These readings train the eye to see given mercy before the appetite can rename life as shortage.

learnItems.title: When mercy makes gratitude honest
learnItems.summary: A brief return to the confession that grace was already working before you noticed it. It lets gratitude become humility, not self-congratulation.

learnItems.title: Gratitude that returns the heart to Naam
learnItems.summary: These readings move gratitude from mood to remembrance, until the heart sees mercy as a summons back to Naam.

learnItems.title: When thanks needs a spine
learnItems.summary: These readings let gratitude mature beyond feeling into discipline that honors the gift by how the day is lived.

learnItems.title: When gratitude becomes dependence
learnItems.summary: These readings let gratitude deepen until the heart stops admiring its own thankfulness and begins depending on mercy.

learnItems.title: When appetite leaves no room for Naam
learnItems.summary: A short bundle for the crowded interior where gold, comfort, taste, and craving all ask to be obeyed. It clears space for Naam before desire names itself as need.

learnItems.title: Greed brought under honorable speech
learnItems.summary: The shabad names greed, falsehood, slander, and anger with unsparing force. These readings bring appetite under the question of what speech can stand at the Lord’s Door.

learnItems.title: When wanting becomes motion
learnItems.summary: These readings expose the restlessness that greed produces when the heart keeps moving because wanting has no end.

learnItems.title: When appetite calls itself seeking
learnItems.summary: These readings separate holy seeking from the appetite that wants another insight, another experience, another thing to own.

learnItems.title: When Hukam leaves ego nowhere to stand
learnItems.summary: A concise return to the Command that holds everyone and everything. It helps the heart stop arguing from the outside and receive the day from within Hukam.

learnItems.title: Hukam inside the ordinary day
learnItems.summary: These readings bring Hukam out of concept and into receiving, acting, and surrendering without arguing with the shape of the day.

learnItems.title: When acceptance slips back into doubt
learnItems.summary: These readings catch the slide from Hukam into suspicion and bring the mind back before doubt can reopen every door.

learnItems.title: When receiving feels too still
learnItems.summary: These readings reveal the moment the heart leaves Hukam because stillness feels too vulnerable, then call it back to faithful presence.

learnItems.title: When the Guru parents the lonely heart
learnItems.summary: A quiet bundle for bringing loneliness into prayer without shame. It follows the helpless child toward the True Guru as protector, mother, father, and living water for the heart.

learnItems.title: Loneliness answered by being held
learnItems.summary: These readings move loneliness toward grace, nearness, and belonging that does not depend on being impressive.

learnItems.title: When loneliness argues with reality
learnItems.summary: These readings bring loneliness under Hukam so the ache can be held without turning the whole day into protest.

learnItems.title: When loneliness drains the day of purpose
learnItems.summary: These readings reconnect loneliness to the rare human chance, so the day is not measured only by who noticed you.

learnItems.title: Mercy that makes courage possible
learnItems.summary: These readings show mercy not as softness alone, but as the force that lets the heart stop living behind armor.

learnItems.title: Mercy for the undeserving hour
learnItems.summary: A brief path for receiving mercy before the heart tries to earn, explain, or control its way back.

learnItems.title: Mercy that teaches the return
learnItems.summary: These readings follow mercy from gift to return, showing how grace gives the heart a way back without making excuses for distance.

learnItems.title: When mercy quiets the frightened body
learnItems.summary: These readings bring fear close to mercy until the body can stop bracing long enough to hear what is true.

learnItems.title: When received mercy opens the hand
learnItems.summary: These readings move from mercy received to forgiveness given, without letting the gift become sentiment only.

learnItems.title: Patience in saintly company
learnItems.summary: A brief path that places impatience near sangat, mercy, and listening until waiting becomes less lonely and more luminous.

learnItems.title: Patience that ripens into honor
learnItems.summary: These readings move waiting from frustration into saintly company, mercy, Naam, and the quiet honor of listening well.

learnItems.title: When waiting softens judgment
learnItems.summary: These readings let patience ripen beyond restraint into a softer judgment of others and of the self.

learnItems.title: Purpose before the day is spent
learnItems.summary: A brief path for remembering that human life is not filler; it is a chance to meet the Lord while the body is still here.

learnItems.title: Purpose that answers the gift of birth
learnItems.summary: These readings follow the rare human chance into Naam, sangat, service, and the urgency of meeting the Lord while there is still time.

learnItems.title: When calling becomes something to possess
learnItems.summary: These readings protect purpose from attachment, where a sacred task quietly becomes a private throne.

learnItems.title: When calling blurs into second-guessing
learnItems.summary: These readings bring the rare human chance back into view when doubt starts dissolving the next faithful step.

learnItems.title: Restlessness brought into company
learnItems.summary: A brief path that stops the wandering mind long enough to find mercy, saintly company, and a truer place to dwell.

learnItems.title: Restlessness that learns to dwell
learnItems.summary: These readings separate holy seeking from agitation and teach the mind to dwell where mercy, sangat, and Naam can actually work on it.

learnItems.title: When motion needs holy company
learnItems.summary: These readings bring restless motion into sangat, where the heart can be steadied by more than its own urgency.

learnItems.title: When motion hides a wound of worth
learnItems.summary: These readings uncover the ache beneath constant motion and return worth to grace rather than achievement.

learnItems.title: Stillness after the false urgency passes
learnItems.summary: These readings bring the overactive search into mercy and saintly company until stillness becomes trustworthy again.

learnItems.title: Belonging without performance
learnItems.summary: These readings bring the lonely or self-conscious heart into sangat where belonging is learned through remembrance, humility, and shared direction.

learnItems.title: Better company before better thinking
learnItems.summary: A brief path for the hour when private thinking has gone stale and the heart needs sangat to remember what it is for.

learnItems.title: Sangat that teaches the life what to become
learnItems.summary: These readings show how atmosphere, placement, and shared remembrance help the rare human chance become a lived answer.

learnItems.title: When belonging becomes management
learnItems.summary: These readings warn that even good company can be turned into a project for control if the self refuses to be corrected.

learnItems.title: Seeking that learns to dwell
learnItems.summary: A brief path for bringing the search back to sangat, Naam, and obedience before spiritual hunger becomes another appetite.

learnItems.title: Seeking that lands in Naam
learnItems.summary: These readings guide spiritual hunger away from constant motion and into the wealth of Naam, patient listening, and saintly company.

learnItems.title: When searching is trying to prove enoughness
learnItems.summary: These readings separate honest seeking from the ache to justify yourself, then return dignity to grace and true wealth.

learnItems.title: Worth held close by grace
learnItems.summary: A brief path that brings worth back from response, status, and success into the nearness of the Lord who holds the humble close.

learnItems.title: Self-worth received, not performed
learnItems.summary: These readings return dignity to the Guru’s gift, the Lord’s nearness, and the humble place where the soul is held without performance.

learnItems.title: Purpose spent in service
learnItems.summary: These readings take purpose out of self-concern and spend it on service that makes the room lighter than it found it.

learnItems.title: Seva without a witness
learnItems.summary: A brief path that clears service of image, hurry, and self-display until the hands can do quiet good.

learnItems.title: Seva that leaves no monument to the self
learnItems.summary: These readings move seva through humility, obedience, honest labor, and rewardless offering until the work reaches beyond self-image.

learnItems.title: When service asks to be paid back
learnItems.summary: These readings guard service at the moment it begins collecting receipts from the people it helped.

learnItems.title: When service teaches acceptance
learnItems.summary: These readings show hidden service training the heart to receive what is given without making every task a negotiation.

learnItems.title: Welcome stronger than shame
learnItems.summary: These readings bring shame toward the Lord who holds the humble close, so return no longer depends on pretending you were never wounded or wrong.

learnItems.title: A rule for tongue and appetite
learnItems.summary: These readings bring speech and appetite under one discipline until the tongue stops carrying greed, slander, and heat.

learnItems.title: Clean the sentence before it hardens
learnItems.summary: A brief path that slows speech under truth, restraint, and honor before words become damage.

learnItems.title: Speech brought back to the Lord’s Door
learnItems.summary: These readings follow speech back to appetite, anger, slander, and truth, then place the tongue under the question of honor.

learnItems.title: When control enters through the tongue
learnItems.summary: These readings expose domination at the level of tone, correction, and pressure before it becomes a whole pattern of control.

learnItems.title: Let the tongue arrive after wisdom
learnItems.summary: These readings teach speech to wait until patience changes the sentence before it leaves the mouth.

learnItems.title: Rest for the overused inner life
learnItems.summary: These readings begin in exhaustion and move toward mercy, holy company, and remembrance that cools the mind and body instead of merely distracting them.

learnItems.title: Buy what can go with you
learnItems.summary: These readings turn trade language toward the soul, teaching the heart to invest in praise, truth, and Naam rather than what cannot travel.

learnItems.title: Panth Prakash
learnItems.summary: English translation of Sri Gur Panth Prakash by Rattan Singh Bhangoo, covering volumes 1 and 2.

learnItems.title: Review saved words
learnItems.summary: Bring saved words back at a steady review pace with pronunciation and meaning.
